items.statement: Full-year FY25 revenue growth guided at 13%-15%
items.quote: Our Quarter 1 revenue grew by 13.1% year-over-year, well within our guided range of 13 %-15% growth for the year.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 EBITDA margin guided at 25%-26%
items.quote: So, we have already guided that we will be in between 25% to 26%. So, we have closed our Quarter 1 at 25%, and we believe that we should go upside to 26% as we go further.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 patient volumes grew 7% YoY with 6% revenue per patient increase
items.quote: Our patient volumes for Quarter 1 grew by 7% year-over-year, with a 6% increase in revenue per patient.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 test volumes grew 10% YoY with 3% revenue per test increase
items.quote: Test volumes grew by 10% year-over-year, with a 3% increase in revenue per test.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA grew 21.2% YoY to Rs 78.2 crore with margin at 25%, up 170 bps
items.quote: Reported EBITDA for the quarter stood at Rs. 78.2 crore as compared to 64.5 crore, a growth of 21.2%. Reported EBITDA margins for Q1 Financial Year ‘2 5 stood at 25% , a growth of 170 basis point year-over-year

items.statement: Q1 FY25 PAT grew 31.3% YoY to Rs 38.1 crore with margin at 12.2%, up 170 bps
items.quote: PAT for the quarter s tood at Rs. 38.1 crore with margin of 12.2% , up from 10.5% for Q1 Financial Year ‘24, which is an increase of 170 basis point year-on-year basis

items.statement: New labs expected to cause ~1% EBITDA dilution in FY25, continuing at lesser amount until FY26
items.quote: As we continue building new labs at a rapid pace this year, we anticipate roughly a 1% EBITDA dilution due to the OpEx losses associated with these new labs.

items.statement: Plan to add 25 labs and 500 centers in FY25 focused on Tier-3 cities
items.quote: We are committed to our expansion strategy of adding 25 labs and 500 centers this financial year with a focus on Tier-3 cities.

items.statement: B2C revenue grew 18.4% YoY to 54% of total revenue; TruHealth up 31%, Specialty up 22%
items.quote: Our B2C revenue growth has been very robust, increasing by 18.4% in Quarter 1. The B2C segment now contributes to 54% of total revenue, up from 51% in Quarter 1, '24, keeping us on track to reach our target of 60% B2C revenue. Our B2C revenues from TruHealth and Specialty grew by 31% and 22% respectively.

items.statement: B2B revenue grew 12.4% YoY; TruHealth and Specialty grew 24% and 11% respectively
items.quote: Our B2B segment has also performed exceptionally well with revenues growing by 12.4% i n Quarter 1 , ‘25. Over the last four quarters, we have increased our market share in the B2B business while maintaining our discount structure, ensuring profitable growth. B2B revenue contributions stood at 37% for Quarter 1

items.statement: TruHealth wellness/illness bundles grew 28% YoY to 17% of total revenue
items.quote: Revenue contribution of TruHealth segment to total revenue has moved up to 17% from 14% indicating a growth of 28% Y-on-Y.

items.statement: Specialty testing contributes 37% of revenue; Specialty + TruHealth together 54%
items.quote: I think we talked, we have mentioned that 37% of the total revenue is coming from the specialized testing, and TruHealth, which is the wellness and illness bundle packaging, has moved up to 17% . So, 54% of the total business is actually coming from Specialty and TruHealth.

items.statement: Consciously defocusing on low-margin institutional government tenders and aggregators
items.quote: We have consciously decided to defocus on our institutional business coming from Government tenders, low margin corporate accounts and aggregators.

items.statement: CAPEX Committee established to oversee infrastructure and technology investments
items.quote: Since we are investing significant capital in infrastructure and technology, we have established a CAPEX Committee to oversee these investments, ensuring efficient capital deployment.

items.statement: Built 79 labs between FY21-FY24; target 90 labs by FY25
items.quote: Meanwhile, we have built 79 labs between FY '21 and FY '24, primarily in Tier-3 and 4 markets. By '25, we will have achieved our goal of establishing 90 labs.

items.statement: No price hike discussion currently; price increases considered annually or once in 18 months
items.quote: If any price increase at this stage or early next year is not under discussion at this point of time. We will take a call at the appropriate time depending upon what's the market conditions as well you know.

items.statement: Pricing power driven by patient criticality and brand trust, not test type; distributor margins rising but Metropolis model is direct-to-consumer
items.quote: So, actually what we find is that pricing is completely impacted by the criticality of the patient. And the more critical the patient, the less chances they are willing to take on something going wrong, and the more chances that they will go to a branded player that they trust, and then price actually has very little meaning.

items.statement: Continuing provisions for Delhi government receivables (Aam Aadmi); volumes down this year
items.quote: So, we continue to do that. I mean, whatever revenues come from that account, we continue to provide for at this point of time and while our efforts on collecting the monies are also on.

items.statement: Net cash surplus of Rs 137 crore as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: Moving on to the balance sheet , we have a net cash surplus of Rs. 137 crore as on 30th June 2024.

items.statement: Actively pursuing bolt-on and strategic acquisitions across three buckets: geographic expansion, technical/medical skills, and turnaround of sub-scale players
items.quote: As we mentioned last quarter, exploring bolt-on and strategic acquisitions remains a key focus, allowing us to enter new markets and acquire new skills. I am personally dedicating a considerable amount of my time in identifying and pursuing acquisitions that I believe will align with our strategy going forward.

items.statement: Launched MILES (Metropolis Institute of Laboratory Education and Skilling) with universities for continuous education of doctors and technologists
items.quote: In line with the Government’s focus on upskilling and workforce development, we have recently launched MILE S, which is Metropolis Institute of Laboratory Education and Skilling, in collaboration with reputed universities to provide continuous education and training for doctors and

items.statement: Created Internal Medical Advisory Board (IMA B) for clinical guidance and innovation
items.quote: We have also created IMA B, which is the Internal Medical Advisory Board, to provide expert guidance on clinical and medical matters. Their insights and guidance will drive innovation and maintain our reputation for clinical excellence.

items.statement: Industry average growth 12.6% in Q1; Metropolis grew 13.1%, outperforming peers
items.quote: In Quarter 1, if I look at the industry average growth of all the operators who have published the results, you know, it stands at 12.6% and we are at 13.1%.

items.statement: Gross margin pressure from new lab ramp-up (higher material cost), new test menu additions, and specialty test launches with low initial volumes
items.quote: While you are right that this whole B2C growth and total growth should add the gross margin, there are certain activities which we are doing, is also taking away like new labs which we are creating. So, that actually has a higher material cost in the initial six to eight month s period because there are very low volumes there and the cost of material is directly proportional to the

items.statement: Competition intensity in Western India/Mumbai stable; no significant pricing competition in last 2-4 quarters
items.quote: See, the Western India, particularly Mumbai, the competition intensity is not any lesser or more than the past, right? I mean, we continue to see a similar amount of rigor from all the competitions. But of course, we have not seen too much competition from the pricing point of view o ver the last two, three, four quarters

items.statement: Focus on AI and digitization for seamless B2C/B2B customer experience and quick query resolution
items.quote: Our aim this year is to create a differentiated brand and empower our services with AI and digitization for a seamless customer experience for both B2C and B2B customers. This will make it easier for customers to access services, schedule appointments, make payments and receive results digitally.

items.statement: Management will wait another quarter to give proper volume growth guidance; growth expected to be slightly lower than earlier targets
items.quote: It will definitely be better than Q1, but still because of global uncertainties, demand in US and Europe is still subdued. So, we haven't been able to get a clear picture of how much we will be Gateway Distriparks Limited & growing. So, we will wait maybe another quarter to give proper guidance, but it is slightly lower than what we were targeting

items.statement: Management targets double-digit volume growth but cannot give specific guidance due to macro uncertainties
items.quote: We will definitely be looking in double digit, but it all depends on the macros.

items.statement: Rail EBITDA per TEU at Rs 9,400; margin slipped due to lower volumes and double stack percentage dropping 2%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin has slipped a little bit because of the low volumes and our double stack percentage has gone down by say 2% this quarter so that reflects on the EBITDA margin

items.statement: CFS EBITDA per TEU improved to Rs 1,350-1,375 from Rs 520 last quarter
items.quote: CFS has maintained the same volume. And I mean the margins on CFS, if you compare them from the last quarter, which was from three digits have gone up to Rs.1,350 - Rs.1,375, last quarter it was Rs.520 only.

items.statement: Double stacking dropped from 39% average last year to 33% in Q1; recovery to 40%+ would directly improve EBITDA
items.quote: So, last year we averaged at about 39%, but this quarter, we were at 33%. As and when the volume cut back and the imbalance within the ports also like Mundra, Pipavav, JNPT our volumes, some were import-heavy, some were export-heavy. Once this number comes back to say 40% which we have done in the past, we have even gone up to 45% in the past it will just straight away add to the EBITDA and the bo

items.statement: Red Sea impact and port congestion continue; slight improvement seen in June-July but US/Europe demand remains subdued
items.quote: Overall that red sea impact still continues, there has been a lot of port congestion at various international ports, vessel schedule has been erratic over the last few months. But slightly we have seen some improvement in June, July is also looking slightly better.

items.statement: Wastepaper imports down 30% at Kashipur and 10% at Ludhiana; bookings improving in July-August
items.value: 30% drop at Kashipur, 10% drop at Ludhiana
items.quote: Kashipur, 85% of the wastepaper is import. So, there has been close to 30% drop in Kashipur. And in Ludhiana we have 20% of our import volumes and there has been almost 10% drop in the import waste paper.

items.statement: Market share in NCR marginally up from ~16% to ~17%; Ludhiana down YoY from 28% to 22.5% but up from Q4; Uttarakhand at ~25%
items.quote: NCR, we have marginally gone up from, say, 16 -point something to almost 17% in Ludhiana, on a YoY basis we have gone down from 28% to 22.5%, but even Q1 is higher than Q4 last year. So, Ludhiana, we started gaining back a little bit of market share and that should improve going forward. Uttarakhand is at about 25% and this fluctuates plus/minus 2% every quarter because the market itself is small.

items.statement: Jaipur terminal expected operational in ~12 months; litigation ongoing but backup plan exists
items.quote: According to our present estimates, we will be operational in about 12 months from now.

items.statement: New ICD planned in North India; land identified but not yet acquired; will be full-fledged ICD with double stacking
items.quote: It will be in north of India. So, it is yet to crystallize, I mean we have identified the land and once we have a deal and we acquire the land that will be the appropr iate time to inform the location

items.statement: Faridabad double stacking work expedited by Indian Railways; expected operational in couple of months
items.quote: They have assured us that they are going to expedite the work and plus due to election also there was some kind of delay, but now Indian Railways has assured us that they have sent a special team and now the work has started in full swing. So, we are expecting that in another couple of months, soon it will be operational.

items.statement: Tax rate expected to stay at 6-7% for next two years
items.quote: Yes, it will stay like this for the next two years at least.

items.statement: Net debt at Rs 245 crores, down significantly from Rs 800 crores peak; gross debt Rs 310 crores
items.quote: Our debt situation is very good right now. I mean we at our lowest net debt to Rs. 245 crores compared to which was at one time Rs. 800 crores or something and even from last quarter last year, if you see it has come down significantly.

items.statement: CFS monetization under evaluation; preparing information memorandum; Nhava Sheva property expected to fetch good valuation
items.quote: We are in the process of putting down everything on paper and preparing information memorandum for any potential buyer to look into.

items.statement: GDL stake in Snowman at 46.4%; can acquire up to 5% per year under creeping acquisition; may exceed 50% by year-end if full 5% acquired
items.quote: See, we are allowed to acquire 5% under creeping acquisition rules. So, last year we acquired 5%, this year we have acquired a little over 1% and we are at 46.4% now and if we complete the full 5% acquisition in this financial year, so we should be ending up little over 50%.

items.statement: Snowman 5PL (distribute) business targets 25%+ YoY growth; grew 29% QoQ and 12% YoY in Q1
items.quote: We have expectations of more than 25% YoY growth on this particular vertical to distribute which is the 5PL vertical. As you see, we have grown 29% over the last quarter and 12% over last year same quarter.

items.statement: Snowman warehousing business expects 12-15% growth in FY25 with new facilities in Lucknow and Kolkata
items.quote: Considering the new facilities which are going to be functional in next month, Lucknow and after that Kolkata, and also some of the lease capacities which we are yet to fully utilize, considering all these, we expect around 12% to 15% growth in warehousing business this year.

items.statement: Snowman warehousing realization up 2.5% YoY; expects another 1% increase next quarter
items.quote: Also, warehousing realization has gone up by 2.5% as compared to last year and we expect it to go by another 1% in the next quarter because some of the price corrections have happened now, which will start yielding in the coming quarter.

items.statement: New 5PL client from ice cream/dairy industry signed; expected to contribute Rs 15-18 crores/quarter from Q2
items.quote: It is from ice cream and dairy industry, and this is expected to contribute anywhere between 15 to 18 crores a quarter.

items.statement: Rail busy season surcharge of 10% passed on to customers; hope for revision to improve competitiveness vs road
items.quote: So, little bit, road does have an advantage with the 10% busy season surcharge that came in. Although we passed it on, we had no choice but to pass i t on to our customers and that's been fully implemented now. But maybe hopefully this can be revised in the near future and then can get a better pricing to make it more competitive

items.statement: DFC Western corridor 93% complete; last 100 km to Vaitarna will take time; commissioning guidance December 2025
items.quote: DFC is giving us guidance for December 2025. And again, the status is the same that 93% of the total WDFC has completed up to Vaitarna and the last leg of 100 kilometers is still going to take a lot of time.

items.statement: EXIM imbalance persists at port level (Mundra imports down, Pipavav imports up) affecting double stacking despite overall 52:48 import:export ratio
items.quote: Yes, but then if you look at within the ports what used to be there like Mundra imports have gone down, Pipavav imports have gone up, so within that there is imbalance. So, for a train running perspective, it is still an imbalance in certain markets.

items.statement: CFS business faces intense competition with no players exiting; management wants to exit but not in a hurry
items.quote: we would definitely want to get out of the CFS business because even though the margins have increased in the first quarter compared to last q uarter of the year, but at the same time, we don't see any uptick on the CFS business because the competition is so intense and there is hardly anyone who has moved out of this business

items.statement: Accounting policy change: consolidator discounts now netted from revenue (Rs 8.43 cr impact); no impact on EBITDA per TEU
items.quote: This is basically a business model done with consolidators, but it was discount being passed on was actually earlier being counted in the revenue. But as per the accounting standard now, that comes under gross revenue, but under net revenue we have to remove this discount. So, it was like a pass-through almost. So, it's gone away from this quarter on.

name: The New India Assurance Company Limited

items.statement: Target double-digit ROE in short to medium term (1-3 years)
items.quote: So, I would like to just inform you that we are committed to have double digit ROE in the short term. So, anything about 10 is what we are targeting to be above 10 in the short term or the medium-term range.

items.statement: Plan to bring down combined ratio significantly in medium term
items.quote: Going forward, we plan to bring down the combined ratio significantly in the medium term so that they're able to be competitive in this current environment as well as have a very win-win situation for the company.

items.statement: Combined ratio at 116.05% for Q1 FY25 vs 115.16% YoY
items.quote: The combined ratio stands at 116.05% as against 115.16% for the corresponding quarter last year and 120.87 for the year ended 31st March 2024.

items.statement: Incurred claim ratio improved to 95.98% in Q1 FY25 from 96.19% YoY
items.quote: The incurred claim ratio has improved to 95.98% for the period ended 30th June 24 as against 96.19% for the corresponding quarter last year and 97.36% for the year ended 31st March 24.

items.statement: Industry grew 13.33% in Q1 FY25; GDP Rs 72,758 crore
items.quote: During the quarter ended June 30, 2024, the industry grew 13.33% with the GDP of Rs. 72,758 crores as against Rs. 64,198 crores for the corresponding quarter of the previous year's.

items.statement: GWP Rs 11,788 crore in Q1 FY25; net earned premium Rs 8,503 crore, up 7.37% YoY
items.quote: The company's GWP for the quarter ended 30th June 24 was Rs. 11,788 crores. Our net earned premium for the quarter ended 30th June 2024 was rupees Rs. 8503 crores, registering a growth of 7.37% year on year.

items.statement: Market share 14.67% as of June 30, 2024; remain market leader
items.quote: Our market share stands at 14.67% as on 30th June 2024 and we continue to be market leader despite the highly competitive environment.

items.statement: Retail health price increase ~25% rolled out last year; further zoning and regulatory hikes this year
items.quote: So, coming to specifics in retail health, there has been a price increase of close to 25 odd percent, which we rolled out last year and this year also because of some zoning related changes, there has been price increase in some zones which has been rolled out.

items.statement: Motor TP no price increase in last 3 years; motor OD price increases rolled out, especially commercial vehicles
items.quote: Coming to motor because there has been no price increase on the motor third party front, we have rolled out some price increases on the motor own damage front in order to cushion the impact so that has been done and that has been done across segments, particularly on the commercial vehicle side.

items.statement: Group health pricing on case-to-case basis; walking away where price not viable
items.quote: On group health, pricing is done on a case-to-case basis depending on how the behavior of the group works and as Mrs. Sushma mentioned earlier, the pricing has been made much more prudent and wherever the price we want is not available, we are happy to walk away.

items.statement: Must comply with master circular changes by 30 Sep 2024; pricing adjustments in ~15% of premium
items.quote: And then now after the master circular, which has come in, there are some 5-6 changes which are introduced and mandated by the regulator for which we have to be compliant by 30th of September'24 to take care of that in some of our products which we had not touched the pricing for maybe over five years or so and which products are actually not very, I would put it this way that they form part of al

items.statement: Focus on retail segment, under-penetrated areas: rural, livestock, tier 2/3 cities, microinsurance, MSME, women, millennials, Gen Z
items.quote: As per our benchmarks by under penetrated areas, we consider potential in the rural sector, livestock insurance tier two and three cities, microinsurance products for low-income groups, MSME sector, women centric products, targeting millennials and the Gen Z.

items.statement: Product mix: Fire 16%, Marine 2%, Motor 22%, Health & PA 50%, Others 10%
items.quote: Our product mix for Fire is at 16%, Marine is 2%, Motor 22%, Health & PA 50% and others at 10%.

items.statement: Launched surety bonds (bid and performance bonds) to support infrastructure
items.quote: The company has a well-diversified portfolio of products, including the recent launches of surety bonds. In fact, New India is one of the few insurers issuing both bid bonds as well as performance bonds, which will support infrastructure growth in the country.

items.statement: Investing heavily in systems, processes, skill development; inducted risk engineers, automobile engineers, doctors
items.quote: We are improvising heavily on our systems and processes. We are investing a lot into skill set development of our employees in order to be able to address issues, you know quickly bring around faster turnaround times in terms of claim service.

items.statement: Premium split 90% domestic, 10% foreign; international operations in 25 developed countries, self-sustaining
items.quote: Yeah. So, our overall premium consists of 10% foreign and 90% domestic.

items.statement: Solvency ratio 1.83x, comfortably above 1.50x threshold
items.quote: The solvency ratio remains comfortably above the threshold of 1.50 times and we are currently at 1.83 times.

items.statement: Investment income weaker YoY due to less equity sold and lower dividend received in Q1
items.quote: Actually, in the first quarter or that profit on sale, we have not sold much equity. Due to that dividend, we received in the first quarter. In the after first quarter also. So we sold less equity after the first quarter and our due to that we realized less profit on sales of equity.

items.statement: Government health scheme loss ratios seasonal; expected to stabilize by year-end
items.quote: Actually, the policy which is there is for a year and in usually in all such policies as the awareness increases and as we encounter different seasons, the claims do change in the numbers and the exposure that is there changes in the time of the year that we talk about; so, usually all such policies they stabilize by end of the year.

items.statement: Medical inflation remains high post-COVID; modern treatments adding cost pressure
items.quote: But at the same time, another challenge or a problem that we encounter all along is the high medical inflation. So, initially it was felt that after COVID the medical inflation would come down, but it has sadly not come down and then to add to it, we also have lot of modern treatments coming up, which are actually quite costly.

items.statement: Recruited large number of doctors; inducted risk engineers, automobile engineers for better risk selection
items.quote: We have inducted a lot of risk engineers, automobile engineers, we have inducted doctors into our workforce and they are working tirelessly and gaining experience each day as we go.

items.statement: Net worth Rs 21,343 crore; net worth including fair value Rs 47,703 crore; investment assets Rs 98,770 crore
items.quote: As on 30th June 2024, the company has a net worth of rupees Rs. 21,343 crores and investment assets standing at rupees Rs. 98,770 crores. The company's net worth including the fair value change account increased from rupees Rs. 44,704 crores in March 24 to rupees Rs.47,703 crores in June 24.

items.statement: Domestic revenue growth guidance of 17% for FY25 maintained
items.quote: Overall FY '25, 17% guidance on growth of domestic market remains. We will achieve that.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin guidance of 15% for domestic business maintained
items.quote: No, no, we maintain our guidance of that 15% because there are lot of other penetration in the new market, other thing will come. So, right now we are holding on to that guidance of 15% on Indian market.

items.statement: Target to increase India revenue share to 70-75% in 3-5 years
items.quote: So, since we are around 60% currently, we have a target of taking it to 70%-75%.

items.statement: Export revenue growth target of 4-5% annually
items.quote: But that will be only compensating our less revenues from Europe and other where it is not growing. So, the export will continuously focus, but we will see that at least we grow by 4% to 5% every year on our export sales.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue target to double in 5 years
items.quote: In five years from now we are doubling. We are doubling top line for sure.

items.statement: Completed Rs 175 crore CAPEX across three Indian manufacturing units
items.quote: We have successfully completed our CAPEX of around 175 crore, which was announced for all three manufacturing units in India.

items.statement: Inaugurated casting flux granules unit at Visakhapatnam with 18,000 MT annual capacity
items.quote: We recently inaugurated state-of-the-art casting flux granules production unit at Visakhapatnam with an annual capacity of 18,000 metric tons.

items.statement: Launched Magnesia Carbon production line with initial 9,000 MT capacity, targeting Rs 100 crore revenue
items.quote: We also launched a new Magnesia Carbon production line, part of our Phase-3 expansion. The facility with an initial capacity of 9,000 metric tons annual will enhance performance, longevity and reliability in high temperature application. This will allow us to generate a revenue of Rs 100 crores.

items.statement: Magnesia Carbon capacity to expand to 24,000 MT by FY26 Q2 with additional Rs 3 crore
items.quote: Plant capacity will be enhanced to 24,000 tons per annum in a year time with further capital outlay of around 3 crores.

items.statement: Odisha land allotment expected within a month for new manufacturing unit
items.quote: Yes, the land allotment is almost nearing because after this election results and everything is over, a new government has come in place. So, we are going to get that within a month's time also.

items.statement: Domestic capacity utilization at 65-70% overall (excluding new Vizag plant)
items.quote: Utilization level is in the range of 65% to 70%, overall basis I am talking about, not product to product.

items.statement: Peak revenue from new flux and Magnesia Carbon lines estimated at Rs 180 crore at full utilization
items.quote: Peak revenue we have already indicated that once when you reach 100% CU capacity utilization of flux plant, that's going to be around 80 crore and Magnesium-Carbon with some debottlenecking and other thing once when we reach, it will be 100 crore. So, it will be totally both the new lines will add 180 crore when we reach full capacity.

items.statement: Domestic steel demand projected at 6-8% growth, driving refractory demand
items.quote: So, steel growth and cement growth are projected, though it has not happened in the same rate in the first quarter, but we are expecting it to pick up, 6% to 8% growth in steel. So, to that extent, our refractory demand also will raise.

items.statement: European steel demand recovery expected from calendar Q4 2024
items.quote: So, I think then German companies will start being good. So, I think, calendar year, if I talk about, then from quarter four onwards, I think demand is expected to pick up in the European steel market.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 12.6% in Q1 FY25, down 11% YoY due to high employee cost, restructuring, and freight
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Quarter 1, FY '25 stood at 12.6%. PAT for the quarter was at 24.7 crore, down by 17% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin at 17.9% in Q1 FY25, down 4% YoY but up 18% QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA for Quarter 1, FY '25 stood at 44.4 crores, down by 4% on year-on-year basis, and up by 18% on Q-on-Q basis. EBITDA margins for Q1 stood at 17.9%.

items.statement: Freight cost impact of Rs 6 crore in Q1 FY25 due to Red Sea crisis
items.quote: So, due to freight, the impact is around Rs. 6 crore.

items.statement: Entered non-ferrous refractory segment with alumina bricks and castables for cement, glass, coke; supplied trial orders to top 2 cement producers
items.quote: Predominantly, it is led by cement now. At the moment, we have already got kind of India's number one and number two cement producers have already given some trial orders and we have already supplied. And to the extent I can say, like around alumina bricks which we are supplying to the tune of 8 crores, the first time we have taken the order and also some castables, monolithic refractories.

items.statement: R&D focus on refractory recycling to reduce input costs and technology transfer from Sheffield Refractories
items.quote: One of key developments will be the initiation of refractory recycling which will significantly reduce input costs and contribute positively to our bottom line. This focus on innovation and cost efficiency is expected to deliver substantial benefits as we move forward, reinforcing our commitment to sustainable growth and profitability.

items.statement: Added new customers in mini steel plant (ESM) segment; increasing share of spend with integrated steel plants
items.quote: Yes, you see, we have added a few, you know, the mini steel plant and particularly with our cost-effective products of this, we name it as electro steel casting, electrical steel making (ESM) sector, where we are fast growing and adding new accounts. But coming to integrated steel plants, it is more of an increase in share of spend than addition of new customers.

items.statement: Mini steel plants contribute ~25% of domestic revenue
items.quote: So, if I talk about domestic kilns, then it would be almost 25%, share of domestic business.

items.statement: Cautious on Liberty Steel Group exposure; provisions taken in December quarter; ArcelorMittal exposure stable
items.quote: In terms of other customers, yes, we are very cautious with respect to Liberty Group, and because of the last quarter we had, in December quarter we had provisions. So, we are very, very cautious on that group, and we have taken the actions in terms of deliveries and payment terms and other things.

items.statement: Export revenue declined 6% YoY to Rs 80.2 crore in Q1 FY25; Europe slowdown primary driver
items.quote: Export business stood at 80.2 crores, saw a decline of 6% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Sheffield Refractories running at ~Rs 45-50 crore quarterly revenue run rate
items.quote: So, Sheffield is now 45-50 crores roughly on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: Company remains net debt-free with Rs 213.4 crore cash and equivalents on consolidated basis
items.quote: With respect to liquidity positions, we remain net debt-free with a strong balance sheet. Cash and cash equivalents stood at 213.4 crore on consol basis as on 30th June 2024.

items.statement: Actively pursuing inorganic growth in India and overseas; no concrete deals to announce
items.quote: Yes, see, we are definitely actively looking forward to our inorganic growth, both in India as well as outside. And as of now, we do not have anything concrete to share with you, but the work is on progress.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis causing freight rate surge from $2,000 to $6,000 impacting export margins and customer deliveries
items.quote: Because of the uncertainty into the freight market, as you know, because of the Red Sea, the freight has gone up from $2,000 to $6,000 in some sectors. So, we can cause a lot of dent in our profitability.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 EBITDA margin expected to cross double digits; H2 FY25 margin guided at 11%

items.statement: Athleisure/apparel launched in ~45 stores with INR 50 lakh inventory test
items.quote: We have taken it in a very small way. Aro und 50 lakhs of inventory we have taken for this introduction and we have launched it in around 40 to 45 stores.

items.statement: Apparel margins lower than footwear but simpler inventory (3 sizes vs 6-7)
items.quote: Apparel is a lesser problem than footwear. In footwear, there are sizes of six, seven sizes are involved, but in apparel we are keeping only three sizes. So I don't think that would be too much constraint for us. But we are taking apparel in a very small way.

items.statement: May reduce MRP on Khadim mother brand lower price points after festive season
items.quote: So maybe we have to take some correction in the MRP for the Khadim brand. But that will be done after the festive season. In the next spring-summer season, we will try to reduce some of the MRP in the mother brand.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven by both retail mix shift and raw material softening
items.quote: It's a mixture of both the things.

items.statement: Average bill value INR 940-945 in Q1 FY25, stable vs last year
items.quote: It was the same last year. In the same range, 900, 920. It was like that. Now it was around 940, 945.

items.statement: Conversion rate improved to 65-70% from pre-COVID 40% due to lower footfall of assured buyers
items.quote: Now the conversion ratio is high because compared to last, when pre-COVID it was around 40% but now it's around 65% to 70%.

items.statement: Punjab government receivable of INR 32 crores expected recovery in FY25
items.quote: It's around INR32 crores.

items.statement: Distributor credit cycle ~45 days, focusing on working capital improvement
items.quote: Distributors' credit cycle is around 45 days. And we are trying to squeeze as much money in the distribution business.

items.statement: De-merger process awaiting NCLT approval, targeting completion by Nov-Dec 2024
items.quote: So we can have the de -merger in the third quarter, maybe in the month of November or December.

items.statement: BIS implementation extended to end of CY2024 for small suppliers (<INR 50 cr turnover)
items.quote: The government still has given an extension till the end of this year. I mean, the normal year not financial year. So after that, let's see what the government says for the smaller suppliers whose t urnover is less, INR50 crores and below

items.statement: Holding market share despite macro challenges; unorganized sector pressure remains short-term
items.quote: We cannot say that we are losing market share. But when there is a festive like Independence Day, in the last week of Independence Day, we have got good sales numbers. So whenever there is a footfall in the market, we are getting the sales.

items.statement: Post de-merger, manufacturing/distribution staff move to new entity; management oversees both
items.quote: Specifically, the manufacturing and the distribution sales people will go to the resulting entity. And the management will look at both the companies. So there will be no new introduction in that company at the management level.

items.statement: Franchisee operating cost increased post-COVID due to lower sales and higher rentals/salaries
items.quote: Because the sales have reduced, that's why the cost has increased. Cost as a percentage has increased. Indrajit Chaudhuri: And also with the inflation coming in, the cost of rentals, the salaries, the other costs has increased

items.statement: Q1 footfalls declined ~20% YoY due to ~70% fewer wedding dates, heatwave, and elections; Q2 footfalls recovering strongly with 10 wedding dates vs negligible last year
items.quote: In this quarter, the sluggishness in the market continued due to the lack of wedding dates. Unlike Quarter 1 of last year, this year the wedding dates in Q1 of this were reduced by almost 70 %, which caused weak consumer walk-ins to our stores.

items.statement: Q2 footfalls tracking higher in July and August; wedding dates in Q2 this year ~10 vs negligible last year; expecting strong recovery
items.quote: We have considerably seen much higher footfall trends in July and in the month of August. So far as of now, we do have wedding dates in this fiscal year. we are sure this quarter is going to be a good quarter, which is going to be a rebound compared to the last quarter that we have.

items.statement: Full-year net profit guidance of INR150 cr not reconfirmed; management will provide better visibility by end of Q2 after new stores ramp
items.quote: by the end of Q2, we should be able to confirm in a much better fashion on the profitability of the current year

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 41.26% in Q1 (+30 bps QoQ, ~98-99 bps YoY); further improvement expected from product mix and supplier terms
items.quote: Despite the weak demand in the ethnic retail space, our company achieved a revenue of INR274 crores with a gross margin of 41.26 percentage, which shows improvement over the last quarter, one of last year.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin single-digit due to negative SSG; expect double-digit EBITDA margin in Q2 as SSG normalizes and new stores contribute
items.quote: In this particular quarter, we have seen a single digit EBITDA margin on account of SSG growth. And apart from that, there is no other specific reason why we should be able to see an EBITDA margin decline. But however, I think quarter two, we should be abl e to recover whatever we have lost in quarter one. And you should be able to see a double digit EBITDA growth for

items.statement: Opened 1 store in Q1; 2 stores delayed due to local clearances (Madurai, Chennai Purasawalkam) — now expected within 1-2 weeks; plan 2-3 new stores in Q2, majority in Q3
items.quote: On the new store rollout front, we have faced some headwinds as two of our new stores that were supposed to open in this quarter did not happen on account of some pending clearances from the local authorities despite completion and ready to open.

items.statement: FY25 store addition guidance maintained at ~90,000 sq ft (delayed by a couple of months); most openings in Q2-Q3, some spill to Q4
items.quote: the guidance of having a 90,000 square feet is what we have promised from the beginning and that's still the case, yes. But what has happened in unforeseen circumstances things have moved down from Q1 to Q2. So, we should be able to se e majority of the stores coming in end of Q2, Q3 and a few stores will also overlap to Q4

items.statement: Total retail area 6.53 lakh sq ft across 61 stores as of 30 Jun; matured store base ~5.9 lakh sq ft; added ~57,000 sq ft over last 5 quarters
items.quote: As of 30th June, the total retail square foot stood at 6.53 lakh square feet with 61 retail stores across four states in the company.

items.statement: Target ~100 stores by end of FY26; 10-15% sq ft addition YoY thereafter; blended revenue per sq ft expected to reach INR28,000-28,500 by FY26
items.quote: We should be able to achieve approximately 100 stores by the year '26.

items.statement: ASP declined ~9% overall, ~12.5% for like-to-like stores in Q1; bill values flat; quantity down 4% YoY
items.quote: See, in terms of the ASPs, I think the overall ASP decline was about 9% for the all stores and for the like-to-like stores, it was around 12 and a half percent.

items.statement: Premiumization via Varamahalakshmi Silks (90% wedding wear) driving mix improvement; converting one Kalamandir store to Varamahalakshmi in Telangana; adding white-label, accessories, lingerie in KLM format
items.quote: one of which includes changing one of the brands from Kalamandir to Varamahalakshmi Silks in Telangana. And this will be ready to open within a week's time.

items.statement: Repeat purchase rate among industry leaders; localized approach adapting to culture and preferences; digital marketing via Salesforce mapping customer journey
items.quote: Our ethnic brands still continue to have one of the industry's leading repeat customer purchase rate. Our brand penetration in the newer markets has been effective.

items.statement: Working capital debt reduced to ~INR150 cr as of Jun end; term loans ~INR30 cr; total debt ~INR180 cr; new store capex breakeven <11 months, working capital breakeven <20 months
items.quote: substantial reduction has taken place in working capital debt. It has come down to approximately INR150 crores as of June end. And the term loans are also in the range of about 30 crores, so the total debt is about INR180 crores only now.

items.statement: Annual interest outflow FY24 ~INR38 cr; Q1 FY25 actual interest outflow INR5 cr (INR5 cr IndAS adjustment); FY25 interest cost expected INR18-19 cr (~50% of FY24)
items.quote: last year the actual interest outflow was around INR38 crores on an annual basis .. Out of the finance cost of Rs.10 crores, the actual outflow on account of interest is only INR5 crores. The other INR5 crores is the IndAS adjustment that we have to take to books.. For the year overall, we are expecting that we should be doing anything where the interest cost should not be more than around INR18 c

items.statement: Same-store sales growth (SSG) negative in Q1; recouping in Q2, expected to neutralize or turn positive; matured store base ~5.9 lakh sq ft
items.quote: Current quarter, they are recouping, yes. It looks that the negative that has come is only restricted to the first quarter. Second quarter onwards, we seem to be experiencing normal operations or EBITDA margins for that matter

items.statement: New Varamahalakshmi stores averaging INR55,000-60,000 revenue per sq ft in first 45 days of Q2 (range INR35,000-60,000 by location)
items.quote: So, overall, when you talk of the average, few stores give below the mark and a few substantially above -, but on average, we are definitely in the range of about 55,000 to 60,000 square feet range.

items.statement: H1 FY25 revenue expected flat to slightly better vs H1 FY24; Q2 revenue growth ~12% YoY implied; EBITDA margin expected to return to ~17% (Q2 FY24 level)
items.quote: At this point in time we can commit that it will be almost closer or slightly less or more than last half year. We should get a better traction because the upward movement has started only for the past 30 days, 40 days and there is about another 45 days to go.

items.statement: Store opening delays from local municipal clearances (2-month delay on 2 stores in Q1); mitigating by stricter compliance monitoring for future openings
items.quote: We had experienced more than a two-month delay on account of this. We are making efforts to clear these bottlenecks and are hoping to get them cleared within a week's time to 10 days' time.

items.statement: Chennai Purasawalkam store chosen despite metro construction; site selected for better parking/traffic; future Chennai sites in areas where metro work complete
items.quote: When we have chosen the choice of Pushwakam, in fact, the metro works have already begun. And we have chosen a place which is convenient and the parking, traffic, etc., was much better, whereby we may slightly have an advantage over the others who are getting blocked in that.

items.statement: Focus remains on Tamil Nadu and Karnataka; exploring 1-2 locations in AP/Telangana; Kerala and Maharashtra later after cluster strategy established
items.quote: Right now, the focus still continues to remain in the sou th of Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. And only one or two locations we are exploring in the current areas of AP and Telangana

items.statement: KLM Fashion Mall format revenue expected flat YoY in FY25; EBITDA margin maintained at historical level; improvement targeted next year via white-label, accessories, lingerie categories
items.quote: KLM, we are expecting that this year, it will be at least a neutral SSE or a little slightly better. Overall, there will not be any degrowth in KLM format for this year.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin expected to improve progressively YoY driven by premium Varamahalakshmi expansion and KLM margin initiatives
items.quote: We should be improving on that because the entire expansion will be going on premium format. So the premiumization will add to the margin profile as well.

items.statement: Global sugar production estimated at 184 MMT vs consumption of 180.8 MMT for SY24-25, showing a surplus
items.quote: As per Czarnikow, the total global sugar production is now estimated at 184 MMT , while consumption is expected to be 180.8 MMT .

items.statement: India sugar production for SY23-24 estimated at 34 MMT, net production close to 32 MMT after ethanol diversion
items.quote: the sugar production for the SY 2023-24 is estimated to be 34 MMT as a few mills are still operational as the special season is in progress in Tamil Nadu. With diversion to ethanol is expected to be just over 2 MMT , the net sugar production will be close to 32 MMT.

items.statement: India closing stock by September 2024 expected at healthy 9 MMT, significantly above 2.5 months consumption norm
items.quote: Considering an opening stock last year of about 5.5 MMT and forecasted domestic consumption of 28.5 MMT, the closing stock by September '24 is expected to be a healthy 9 MMT.

items.statement: FRP increased by Rs. 25 per quintal for SY24-25, no policy clarity on ethanol diversion rollback or MSP revision
items.quote: The FRP increase which has already been announced for SY 2024-25 by Rs. 25 a quintal will also attract more farmers to plant sugarcane which aug urs well for the industry

items.statement: No policy clarity on rollback of ethanol diversion and revision of MSPs despite industry representations
items.quote: We still don't have any policy clarity with regard to the rollback of ethanol diversion and revision of MSPs despite number of representations from the industry.

items.statement: Standalone Q1 FY25 revenue Rs. 751 crore up 7.58%, EBITDA loss Rs. 28.59 crore vs loss Rs. 14.63 crore, loss after tax Rs. 78.59 crore vs Rs. 45.77 crore
items.value: Revenue 751 cr, EBITDA -28.59 cr, PAT -78.59 cr
items.quote: The standalone revenue from operations for the quarter ended 30th June 2024 at Rs. 751 crores registered an increase of 7.58% as against Rs. 698 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. The EBITDA for the quarter ended was loss of Rs. 28.59 crores as against the loss of Rs. 14.63 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. The standalone loss after tax for the quarter

items.statement: Cane cost increased to Rs. 3,491/MT from Rs. 3,267/MT previous year
items.quote: So, overall cane cost is about Rs. 3,491 per MT and last corresponding year was Rs. 3,267 per MT.

items.statement: Refinery long-term loan Rs. 200 crore unchanged, short-term loan reduced to Rs. 220 crore from Rs. 596 crore
items.quote: So far as long-term loan of the refinery is concerned, including EID Loan is Rs. 200 crores. The same was Rs. 200 crores in the last year. As far as the short-term loan is concerned it was about Rs. 220 crores for the current quarter as against the previous year's corresponding quarter of Rs. 596 crores.

items.statement: Short-term borrowings increased due to working capital needs, inventory up ~Rs. 300 crore year-on-year
items.quote: term loan is basically the working capital. Since our networking capital has gone up, thereby, your short-term loans also have gone up. Because even if you look at inventory also, inventories has gone up around Rs. 300 crores, in line with the short-term loans also increase

items.statement: Aspire to match last year's crushing numbers in current fiscal despite Tamil Nadu challenges
items.quote: In the fiscal that we are currently in, we would aspire to almost match last year's number; however, there could be some challenges in Tamil Nadu on that, but we are working towards trying to match last year's number.

items.statement: Nutra Europe certification expected in next couple of weeks, billing to Europe from Q3 FY25 onwards
items.quote: So, yes, we do have some good news that is coming through in the next couple of weeks. So, I think we should be able to start billing to Europe towards the end of sort of Q3. Gautham: Q3 you said? Muthiah Murugappan: I think we should be billing from Q3 onwards

items.statement: Tamil Nadu recovery challenged by last year's deficient monsoon, El Nino impact takes 24 months to normalize, Karnataka area under cane slightly down but yields strong
items.quote: The deficient rainfalls of last year have certainly had an impact on Tamil Nadu. We are already seeing that, Venkat talked about the lower recoveries that we are experiencing, and it is only now that once the monsoons have picked up, we are starting to see some plant coming in. Tamil Nadu will remain challenging.

items.statement: Distillery margins fallen from target 20-21% EBITDA to single digits due to no ethanol price increase for sugarcane feedstock despite FRP hike
items.quote: When I talked about our dis tillery segment margins, we would have been very happy with 20 %-21% EBITDA business. That is what we were really building towards in the old policy framework. But I think once there was a reconsideration of this and the fact that prices were not taken up, these margins have fallen substantially and gone in sort of closer to single digit

items.statement: Brown sugar 'Amrit' launched at Rs. 80/kg under Parry Gold brand as penetrative pricing vs existing Rs. 100/kg product
items.quote: So, we are looking at pricing the new brown sugar which is nothing but your crystal brown sugar under the ‘Par ry Gold’ brand name and this is priced lower more as a penetrative pricing into the market in order to generate more trials from consumers

items.statement: Green Grow media from bagasse for soilless growing medium, large export and domestic potential, product and customer development ongoing
items.quote: The Green Grow Media is from bagasse, the residual bagasse. It is a soil-less growing medium, which you would find in greenhouses, got a lot of potential in the export market and in India. Product development and customer development is ongoing.

items.statement: Expects capacity utilization close to 75% for full year FY25 despite weak global steel demand
items.quote: For Q1 '25, which means April, May, June we were close to 80% capacity utilization, and we hope to be close to 75% for the full year despite steel not doing very well in the world.

items.statement: Graphite anode plant capex spent so far is around INR 60 crores, mainly for land and pre-operative expenses
items.quote: So on the graphite anode part of it, the total capex that the company has done till now is around INR 60 crores, out of which between INR 30-35 crores is purely on account of land.

items.statement: Graphite electrode expansion from 80,000 to 100,000 tons per annum is fully complete and all new facilities are running smoothly
items.quote: As you are aware, our expansion from 80,000 to 100,000 tons is fully complete and all the new facilities are running very smoothly.

items.statement: Over 100 million tons of new greenfield electric arc furnace capacity announced globally, with ~64 million tons likely operational by 2027
items.quote: As we speak, more than 100 million tons of new Greenfield capacities have already been announced, which will be in operation between now and 2030, out of which about 64 million tons is likely to be in operation by as early as 2027.

items.statement: Electrode demand likely to increase by 100,000 to 125,000 tons in next 3 years due to new EAF capacities
items.quote: So that is likely to give a boost to electrode demand to the extent of 100,000 to 125,000 tons in the next 3 years or so.

items.statement: Spread between electrode prices and needle coke prices narrowed, pressuring margins over last 6-7 quarters
items.quote: But the spread between electrode prices and needle coke prices did narrow down, bringing pressure on margins as is evident when you look at our margins for the last 6-7 quarters.

items.statement: Anode project EBITDA margin estimated at 30-35% at $10,000/ton anode price, falling to ~20% at $7,000/ton, but could reach 25-26% with lower power costs
items.quote: So right now, I mean it's just a temporary blip right now, which you -- if you see at USD10,000 per ton, our EBITDA margin was coming to around 30%, 35%. And the same prices go down to USD 7,000, the EBITDA margins go down to around 20%.

items.statement: Needle coke prices corrected through past year; electrode pricing remains under pressure due to reduced demand from Chinese steel exports
items.quote: The electrode pricing continues to remain under pressure due to reduced demand. The needle coke prices kept correcting through the past year due to difficult market conditions.

items.statement: Graphite anode powder prices fell from $10,000-12,000/ton to $6,000-8,000/ton as battery prices dropped from $85-100/kWh to $50-60/kWh
items.quote: Today when the prices have gone down for the batteries up to $50 to $60 per KWH, the price of anode too today, you are getting between $6,000 to $7,000 per KWH depending from application to application.

items.statement: Power cost is 30-35% of variable cost for anode plant; negotiating with state governments for cheaper power (targeting INR 5-5.5/kWh vs current higher rates)
items.quote: We are trying to renegotiate with the state government and different other state governments in India on the power prices because power constitutes around 30% to 35% of the variable cost in this particular project.

items.statement: Current HEG power cost INR 5-5.5/kWh at existing site due to thermal plant shutdown subsidy; not automatically transferable to new anode plant location
items.quote: HEG's current cost of between INR5 to INR5.5 is on the basis of HEG shutting off its thermal power plant. So when HEG shuts off its thermal power plant, in lieu of that, the government has given a subsidy and giving power at INR5 to INR5.5.

items.statement: Anode customers like Exide and Ola require 15-18 month qualification process; once qualified, switching is difficult due to 42 raw materials in battery production
items.quote: So once they select between an HEG or an Epsilon or Himadri or any other company that they want to buy the anode from, then it is very difficult or I'd rather say, not worthwhile to try and consider a change.

items.statement: Chinese anode producers selling below variable cost due to overcapacity; China has 90% of global anode manufacturing
items.quote: Right now, they would be importing this from China or any other company. I mean, obviously, China has 90% of the anode manufacturing around the world.

items.statement: Scheme of arrangement for restructuring and demerger progressing with SEBI and stock exchanges; expects completion by middle of next year after NCLT approval
items.quote: After the stock exchange approval, the scheme will also require approval from the NCLT, National Company Law Tribunal. We expect the process to be completed by middle of next year.

items.statement: GST show cause notice for INR 282 crores received; company evaluating and will respond shortly, prima facie demand not correct
items.quote: We are currently evaluating it, and our legal team will be responding to the authorities. Prima facie the demand which has been provided and asked by the authority is not correct.

items.statement: Company is long-term debt-free with treasury of INR 917 crores as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: The company is long-term debt-free and had a treasury size of nearly INR917 crores as on June 30, 2024.

items.statement: HEG Greentech will hold 51% of Malana Power (100 MW) and AD Hydro (200 MW) post restructuring; Statkraft holds 49%
items.quote: So today when the entire restructuring will be completed, HEG Greentech will hold 51% of Malana Power, 49% is held by the Statkraft. And then there is 100% companies underneath the Malana Power, which is AD Hydro.

items.statement: India battery production capacity projected at 80-130 GWh by 2030 per NITI Aayog, implying 80,000-130,000 tons anode demand
items.quote: But the NITI Aayog really says that by 2030, we will have a minimum of 80 gigawatt hour to a maximum of 130 gigawatt hours of battery production in India. That would mean 1 gigawatt hour would mean 10,000 tons of anode requirement.

items.statement: Mark-to-market loss of INR 30-31 crores on GrafTech equity investment booked under other expenses in Q1 FY25
items.quote: So it will be in between INR30 crores to INR31 crores.

items.statement: GrafTech received NYSE delisting notification due to stock price below $1; company believes mitigation possible via reverse split or new investment
items.quote: The exchange has given them the time line for 6 months. And I believe, this is our understanding, they have different ways of getting it -- keeping it in the exchange itself because we understand they are looking for an investment.

items.statement: Anode plant commissioning pushed to FY26-27; all machinery orders ready, civil designs complete, awaiting power cost negotiations with state governments
items.quote: We've kind of pushed forward our commissioning target for this particular plant. That's only on account of two things. We are absolutely ready with all the machinery that has to be placed in terms of the orders.

items.statement: Exports 65-70% of production to 30-35 countries for last 25-35 years; well positioned to serve global EAF capacity growth
items.quote: As we have been exporting about 65% to 70% of our production to more than 30-35 countries for a very long time, we are in a good position to meet this increasing demand for our products all over the world.

items.statement: No management changes mentioned; leadership team includes Chairman Ravi Jhunjhunwala, Vice Chairman Riju Jhunjhunwala, ED Manish Gulati, CFO Om Prakash Ajmera, CSO Puneet Anand, GM Finance Ravi Tripathi
items.quote: We have with us Mr. Ravi Jhunjhunwala, Chairman, Managing Director and CEO; and Mr. Riju Jhunjhunwala Vice Chairman. Along with their colleagues, Mr. Manish Gulati, Executive Director; Mr. Om Prakash Ajmera, Group CFO, Mr. Puneet Anand, CSO; and Mr. Ravi Tripathi, GM Finance.

items.statement: Pumped hydro project at Himachal plants stalled due to state government demanding additional 15-20% free power, making it unviable
items.quote: Himachal Electricity Board wants another 15%, 20% free power out of this added generation of pumped storage. So after giving that 15%, 20% a second time, it doesn't remain viable.

items.statement: BESS system costs fell from INR 2.5 crore/MW to INR 1.25-1.3 crore/MW; SECI tenders for hybrid solar-wind-BESS at INR 3.40/kWh for 20 years
items.quote: So the cost of BESS systems, which used to be INR2.5 crores per megawatt has come down to around INR1.25 crores per megawatt.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance ₹370-380 crore, ~10% growth; FY26 target to cross ₹500 crore
items.quote: This year, we are looking at anywhere between ₹370 crores to ₹380 crores, including our Jaipur hotel. Like last year, our top line had been ₹312 crores. But if we include Jaipur, it will become around ₹340 crores. So, this year, we are looking at ₹370 crores to ₹380 crores, our top line growth of arou nd 10%, okay? And as far as next year is concerned, our target is to cross ₹500 crores

items.statement: FY25 PAT guidance ₹55-58 crore (IndAS); FY26 target around ₹70 crore
items.quote: Yes, this year PAT, we would be closing somewhere , because see the fact of IndAS effect, because of the Bombay property will come. So, it is very difficult to really analy se the effect of the IndAS right now. However, we are looking at a PAT of around ₹55 crores to ₹58 crores in this year. And next year around, we'll be crossing around ₹70 crores

items.statement: Target 200 operating hotels by Feb 21, 2026; revenue ~₹550 crore and PAT ~₹100 crore by FY26
items.quote: Well, you see, we're at 107 operating assets. I think if you look at there is an internal target of February 21, 2026, right, where we want to try and hit the 200-hotel mark, okay? That's the target for Feb 21, 2026, right? But that 200-hotel mark, you're really looking at what is the mix, right? We're looking at what sort of revenue numbers, we should be at the 550-odd mark. We should be inching

items.statement: Goa expansion ~50 rooms at ₹25-30 crore; Yelahanka resort ~₹12 crore
items.quote: See, there in Goa, we a re planning to add about 50 rooms. So, we're expecting a project cost of about ₹25 crores to ₹30 crores in Goa. And as far as resort is concerned, it's going to be about ₹12 crores or

items.statement: 1,900 keys across 26 hotels to open in FY25; mostly managed, one revenue-share (Gurgaon 124 rooms), one owned (Mumbai ~300 rooms)
items.quote: See as far as the deals are concerned, see the total upcoming keys is around 1,900 keys, okay, which is in 26 hotels. And most of it are managed only except two hotels, one is in Gurgaon, which is coming as revenue share and one i n Mumbai, which is owned. Otherwise, all are managed

items.statement: July like-for-like growth 6-8%; resort occupancy returning; corporate and group demand picking up post-elections
items.quote: July saw some hangover from June. So, we've had some pickup in July. And certainly, be tween 6% and 8% growth is occurring that we can see like -for-like in the quarter. What also is the case is that we're seeing some bringing back of resort occupancy as well. So, you've got resort occupancy coming back through the system. We've also got some groups coming back through the system post-election and

items.statement: ARR growth 6-8% across portfolio in current quarter, varying by micro-market (Pune, Mumbai, Gurgaon stronger)
items.quote: Correct, although I would have to say to you that it's not flat across the board, because we have such an array of assets from resorts to hill stations to city locations three, four, and five stars. So, when I give you that direction, it's across the board, higher in some locations and lesser in others.

items.statement: Room renovations to continue for next two quarters, causing revenue dip but higher ARR when rooms return online
items.quote: See, room renovation will continue in the next two quarters also because we can't do it at a time. Because it's running an operating hotel, we can't shut the hotel and do it. So, we're doing it in a phase manner. So, it will have some impact on the next two quarters also. Ayesha: Okay. Thank you. Arjun Baljee: But I just want to add to that, the replacem ent, when you take away old rooms and you s

items.statement: Mumbai hotel IndAS lease impact ~₹7-8 crore/year (₹2.5-3 crore/quarter) due to high lease rent
items.quote: See, it all depends when the hotel opens, okay? So that pro rata period will come. But because the lease rent there is very high. So, the effect of that will be also ₹7 crores, ₹8 crores so definitely, it will come in a year. And if you take quarter-wise, around ₹2.5 crores to ₹3 crores per quarter, it will come the IndAS effect.

items.statement: Revenue target of INR700 crores for FY25
items.quote: we have given the total target of INR700 crores this year by March 25 and we are working seriously on that subject and we hope we will be able to achieve the target of INR700 crores top line.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 18-19% for FY25
items.quote: And if we look into financial year '25, we would be around 18%, 19% EBITDA margin. Overall basis.

items.statement: UPSRTC contract worth INR60 crores over 5 years
